open_points.subject: A17 IPv4 address grammar
open_points.text: Written as text, an IPv4 host is four decimal numbers joined by dots
open_points.question: Must IPv4 octets use the canonical ASCII form without leading zeroes, or are forms such as 127.000.000.001 accepted; and must each number explicitly be from 0 through 255?
options: Accept any four ASCII decimal integers in the range 0–255, including leading zeroes
Accept only four canonical ASCII decimal integers in the range 0–255, with no leading zeroes except the number 0
Delegate acceptance to the chosen IP-address parser
open_points.default_guess: Accept only canonical ASCII octets from 0 through 255.

witness.initial: Registry is stopped and otherwise has a valid complete configuration.
events: The owner configures the owner address as 127.000.000.001:8781 and starts Registry.
outcomes: Registry accepts the address and listens on 127.0.0.1:8781.
Registry rejects the address as malformed and names the owner address.

open_points.subject: A17 address digit alphabet
open_points.text: the port is decimal digits without a leading zero
open_points.question: Does “decimal digits” mean only ASCII 0–9, or every Unicode decimal-digit character accepted by the implementation language?
options: Only ASCII digits 0–9 are valid
Unicode decimal digits are valid when they represent a number in range
Acceptance follows the selected numeric parser

witness.initial: Registry is stopped and all configuration except the owner address is valid.
events: The owner supplies 127.0.0.1:٨٧٨١, whose port uses Arabic-Indic decimal digits, and starts Registry.
outcomes: Registry reads the digits as 8781 and starts.
Registry rejects the address as malformed and names the owner address.

open_points.subject: A17 IPv6 address grammar
open_points.text: an IPv6 host the bracketed form any IPv6 text form names
open_points.question: Which IPv6 textual grammar is meant, including whether scoped zone identifiers, embedded dotted-decimal tails and other implementation-specific forms are accepted?
options: Accept only RFC IPv6 address text without a zone identifier, enclosed in brackets
Also accept scoped forms such as [fe80::1%eth0]
Use whatever forms the selected IP-address parser accepts
open_points.default_guess: Accept standard IPv6 address text, including embedded dotted-decimal tails, but reject zone identifiers unless they are specified separately.

witness.initial: Registry is stopped on a host with interface eth0 and otherwise valid configuration.
events: The owner configures the owner address as [fe80::1%eth0]:8781 and starts Registry.
outcomes: Registry accepts the scoped address and opens the listener on eth0.
Registry rejects the address as malformed and names the owner address.

open_points.subject: A17 IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses
open_points.text: An IPv6 address is listened on for IPv6 alone, never for IPv4 connections mapped onto it. Written as text, an IPv4 host is four decimal numbers joined by dots and an IPv6 host the bracketed form any IPv6 text form names, each read into the address it names
open_points.question: Is an explicitly configured IPv4-mapped IPv6 address such as [::ffff:127.0.0.1] valid, or must it be refused because mapped IPv4 connections are forbidden?
options: Reject every IPv4-mapped IPv6 configured host
Accept it as an IPv6 address but keep the socket IPv6-only
Treat acceptance as platform-dependent if the operating system cannot bind it with IPv6-only enabled

witness.initial: Registry is stopped and otherwise has a valid complete configuration.
events: The owner configures the owner address as [::ffff:127.0.0.1]:8781 and starts Registry.
outcomes: Registry accepts the syntactically valid IPv6 address and attempts an IPv6-only bind.
Registry refuses the address because it denotes an IPv4-mapped address.

open_points.subject: A17 parsed address representation
open_points.text: each read into the address it names; the port is decimal digits without a leading zero. The configuration hands each address on as its host and port.
open_points.question: In what exact types and forms are the host and port handed on: original strings, canonical unbracketed host text plus an integer port, or a typed binary IP address and integer port?
options: Preserve the original host spelling and decimal port text
Pass canonical unbracketed IP text and an integer port
Pass a typed IPv4/IPv6 address object and an integer port
open_points.default_guess: Pass a typed IP-address value and an integer port, retaining the family explicitly.

open_points.subject: A17 closed-listener rebinding
open_points.text: no port sharing; rebinding a port a closed listener left is not sharing
open_points.question: Is immediate rebinding of a recently closed listener required to succeed when the operating system can permit it, or is it merely allowed and a start may fail without a rebinding socket option?
options: Require the safe rebinding option needed for immediate restart, while forbidding active-listener sharing
Do not require any rebinding option; failure to bind stops the start
Leave the result to operating-system defaults
open_points.default_guess: Enable only the platform option required for safe rebinding after close, while explicitly disabling active port sharing.

witness.initial: A prior Registry listener has closed, but the operating system still retains connection state for its port.
events: The owner immediately starts Registry again with the same configured address.
outcomes: Registry uses safe closed-listener rebinding and starts.
Registry uses no rebinding option, cannot open the listener, and stops the start.

open_points.subject: A17 overlapping wildcard listeners
open_points.text: Registry opens each listener for itself alone, never with an option that lets another active socket bind the same endpoint
open_points.question: Does “the same endpoint” include overlapping wildcard and specific-address binds on the same port, or only an identical host-and-port bind tuple?
options: Any wildcard/specific-address overlap on a port counts as sharing and must be prevented
Only an identical normalized IP address and port counts as the same endpoint
Use the operating system's definition of conflicting binds
open_points.default_guess: Treat every wildcard/specific-address overlap that can receive the same traffic as forbidden sharing.

events: The owner configures Registry to listen on 0.0.0.0:8781 and starts it on a platform that can permit overlapping binds with reuse options.
outcomes: Registry treats the overlap as endpoint sharing and stops the start.
Registry treats the bind tuples as different endpoints and starts.
witness.observer: The owner and clients connecting to port 8781

open_points.subject: A17 formal invariant and Required tests
open_points.question: Which Required tests item must show that the newly added no-active-port-sharing and IPv6-only requirements are part of the passed checks before serving?
options: Extend Required test 8 to exercise active bind overlap, safe closed-listener rebinding and rejection of IPv4-mapped connections
Add a separate Required tests item for listener exclusivity and IPv6-only behavior
Declare that these listener properties are outside checks_passed(config) and state their own formal invariant and test
open_points.default_guess: Add a separate Required tests item proving listener exclusivity and IPv6-only behavior before Registry serves.

open_points.subject: A21 security review after the A17 change
open_points.text: 2. A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
open_points.question: Where is the reopened review of the new A17 address grammar, IPv6-only listening and port-sharing rules recorded, and what outcomes does it give for every category that names A17?
options: Reperform and record the authentication_credential_abuse and secrets category reviews for the complete revised A17
State explicitly that the existing 2026-11-11 review was performed after and includes all of these additions
Leave the earlier review standing without reopening it
open_points.default_guess: Reperform and record the two categories that reference A17.

witness.initial: A21's latest recorded review is closed, and its authentication_credential_abuse and secrets categories reference A17.
events: A17 is changed after that review to add address grammar, IPv6-only listening and active-port-sharing rules.
A later agent decides whether A21 remains complete.
outcomes: A21 rule 2 reopens the review, so those categories are reviewed again before A21 is closed.
The existing dated review is silently treated as covering the later A17 change, so no new review is recorded.
witness.observer: The owner and the security-review gate
